critiques.summary: H3 (auth-service-local CPU saturation, ~06:52Z onset) is the only surviving hypothesis and its mechanism is grounded at each hop: CPU steps 37%->97% in the same 240s bucket as p99 (88ms->3.8s) and is pinned through 08:59Z (F8,F9); the 503s are self-generated accept-queue overflows on POST /v1/auth/login (F10); the request-rate rise coincides with, not precedes, onset (F27,F39,F40,F41), so load is an effect (retry amplification mirrored at api-gateway, F42,F43). The shared-cache branch (H2/H4) is now contradicted on both sides: redis-cache is flat on all five stored metrics at 06:30-07:15Z (F31-F37) and all four consumers except auth-service are clean, only the api-gateway->auth-service call chain degrades (F29,F44,F45,F48). H1's bcrypt mechanism is falsified by zero auth-service deploys (F3,F16). No competing origin remains, and no further tool calls are available, so accept rather than inconclusive. Confidence capped at 0.72 because H3 is a negative/local finding reached by elimination: the specific CPU-bound work is unresolved, the pre-onset baseline 00:00-03:00Z is permanently unavailable (F38), and the 'no autoscaling/throttle at onset' assumption was never checked.

challenges.issue: The claim 'auth-service-local, no external load or change driver' is established by elimination (redis flat, other consumers clean, no pre-onset rate ramp) rather than by positive proof of the auth-service-internal trigger. The hypothesis' own statement admits the CPU-bound work (hashing path vs lock/queue spin vs retry feedback) is unresolved, so the origin is pinned but the mechanism is not.

Stated assumption 'no autoscaling, scale-out, node-placement or cgroup CPU-throttle event fired at ~06:52Z' was never checked. If a throttle or capacity event did fire at onset, the 'static capacity floor' framing breaks and the origin shifts off auth-service. This is an unqueried alternative, not a refuted one.

The 'no genuine pre-onset surge' premise is verified only from 03:00Z (F38: the series itself begins at 03:00Z; two narrow 00:00-03:30Z queries returned the same first point). The 00:00-03:00Z baseline is permanently unverifiable, so 3 of the 6.9 pre-onset hours are unchecked.

The pre-onset request_rate is ~400 req/s but the discharge is attributed to retries; with no per-endpoint breakdown, the assertion that the post-onset 1470-1540 req/s (and the gateway's 4.9k) is retry amplification stays an inference from mirrored timing rather than a measured retry source.

Its operative transmission hop ('CSV endpoint drives substantial NEW shared-cache/ledger-db load') was never measured and could not be measured with available tooling (agent had no metric timeseries; redis-cache/ledger-db expose only whole-component aggregates). Contradicted rather than tested.

redis-cache has no restart/failover/replication metric and no latency metric, so a silent failover cannot be excluded from cache-side telemetry; it is excluded only indirectly by flat hit_ratio/connected_clients and by the flat consumer-side latency of the other three consumers.

Rejected on absence of evidence: zero auth-service deployments (F3/F16) and the only config change is log-level (F2/F15). Residual gap: a bcrypt cost change delivered as an env-var/flag not modelled as a config_change could theoretically be missed, so the rejection rests on tool completeness.
